summary.summary_text: Tokyo Cement manufactures and sells cement in Sri Lanka -- the country's largest cement producer and its only listed one -- earning through volume (tonnage) x price per bag, sold through a dealer/distribution network (Annual Report 2023/24, Chairman's Message; Annual Report 2021/22, p.31). The single biggest dependency is construction-sector demand, which is itself gated by government infrastructure spending and lending rates (Annual Report 2023/24, Management Discussion and Analysis). Group revenue swung from LKR 35.8Bn (FY2020) up to LKR 56.5Bn (FY2023) and back down to LKR 49.8Bn (FY2024), tracking construction-cycle demand rather than a steady growth trend. Profitability has been considerably more volatile than revenue: FY2022 was a reported Group loss (LKR -0.36Bn) driven by a large exchange loss following the 2022 Rupee float, even though revenue grew 22% that year (Annual Report 2021/22, Chairman's Message) -- a clear illustration of currency/import-cost exposure sitting on top of the underlying cement business.
summary.gaps_note: FY2025 (year ended 31 March 2025) not included: the FY2025 annual report exists in the document library (collected live, source_id 51996) but was not read for this pilot summary. The most recent interim report on file (period ended 31 December 2025) is an image-based PDF with no extractable text layer, so its figures could not be pulled automatically -- flagged here rather than estimated. FY2019 figures were visible in the FY2019/20 annual report but that report's PDF has font-encoding corruption on some numeric cells; only the unambiguous chart callouts (FY2019 Group revenue ~LKR 38.5Bn, EPS -1.23) were legible and are not included in the row-level table above to avoid citing a partially-corrupted source with false precision.

financials_interim.notes: Standalone (Company) column. EPS cross-check (203,784k / 441,045,000 shares = Rs.0.46) and balance-sheet identity both tie out exactly. Company standalone Profit from Operations fell -30% YoY (604,656 vs 864,101) and PAT fell -55% (203,784 vs 452,852), far worse than the Group's roughly flat PAT (-5%) -- the subsidiaries (notably Tokyo Eastern Cement and Tokyo Super Aggregate) evidently absorbed a large part of the standalone decline, cushioning Group results. short_term_borrowings = current Interest Bearing Borrowing (8,948,023) + Bank Overdrafts (707,697); long_term_borrowings = non-current Interest Bearing Borrowings (4,472,605, of which Rs.1,350Mn per Note 9 is an intercompany loan from subsidiary Tokyo Eastern Cement). Lease creditors excluded from borrowings, consistent with the Group row.

Single-segment cement manufacturer/aggregate producer; no segmental note disclosed (Group accounts consolidate Tokyo Cement Power, Tokyo Eastern Cement, Tokyo Super Aggregate (51%), Tokyo Supermix, Tokyo Cement Industrial Park). EPS cross-check (attributable PAT 636,147k / 441,045,000 total shares = Rs.1.44) and balance-sheet identity (assets = liabilities + equity, exact to the rupee both periods) both tie out cleanly -- no column-swap found in this filing. short_term_borrowings = current 'Interest Bearing Borrowing' (11,465,788) + Bank Overdrafts (1,159,502); long_term_borrowings = non-current 'Interest Bearing Borrowings' only. Lease creditors (current 108,465 / non-current 661,329) excluded from borrowings as they are finance lease obligations, not loans/debentures. Note 9 discloses Rs.1,350Mn of the Company's interest bearing borrowings is an intercompany loan payable to subsidiary Tokyo Eastern Cement -- this nets out at Group level so does not distort the Group borrowings figure used here.

thesis.thesis_text: Tokyo Cement is Sri Lanka's largest and only listed cement producer -- a genuine market-leadership position -- but FY2024 Group results were weak: revenue fell 11.8% and PAT fell 51.5% YoY, with leverage rising (debt/equity 0.47x, Net Debt/EBITDA up from 0.76x to 1.67x). Operating cash flow did swing positive (-7.5bn to +5.6bn), suggesting some of the earnings weakness is working-capital timing rather than a structural break, but this can't be confirmed without a more recent filing. At 15.3x trailing P/E despite the earnings decline, the stock does not look statistically cheap on an earnings basis, though its 0.89x P/B is below book (Annual Report FY2024, p.104-107).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Governance & Risk is also necessarily thin -- no circulars/disclosures feed exists (deliberately disabled this session), so insider transactions, board changes, and rights issues cannot be verified directly; the score below reflects only what's visible in audited financial statements and public market data.

financial_quality.rationale: FY2024 Group ROE just 8.8%, ROA 4.8%, net margin 4.9% -- materially weaker than the other pilots. Current ratio a tight 1.08x and debt/equity 0.47x, the highest leverage in this pilot set. Net Debt/EBITDA rose from 0.76x to 1.67x YoY.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group revenue DECLINED 11.8% YoY (56.5bn to 49.8bn) and PAT fell 51.5% (4.99bn to 2.42bn) -- a genuinely weak year, though cash from operations swung from -7.5bn to +5.6bn, suggesting a working-capital-driven earnings dip rather than a structural collapse.

valuation.rationale: P/E 15.3x looks expensive given the declining-earnings trend just described; P/B 0.89x (below book) is a mitigating cheap signal. Dividend yield 2.98% with 45.6% payout. Mixed: cheap on assets, not cheap on trailing earnings momentum.

business_quality.rationale: Sri Lanka's largest and only listed cement producer -- a genuine domestic market-leadership moat, but cement demand is directly tied to the construction/infrastructure cycle, which appears to have been in a down-year per the FY2024 figures.

governance_risk.rationale: Leverage increased YoY and the earnings decline reduces headroom; no disclosures feed to verify recent corporate actions. Cyclical industry exposure is itself a risk factor, not just a governance one.

key_reasons: Largest and only listed cement producer in Sri Lanka -- a real domestic moat
P/B of 0.89x is below book value, a cheap signal even as trailing earnings weakened
Operating cash flow swung sharply positive YoY, suggesting some FY2024 earnings weakness may be working-capital timing rather than structural
watch_factors: Revenue and PAT both declined double-digit/double-digit-plus YoY -- this data is from FY2024 and may already be stale; a more recent annual report should be sourced to confirm whether the trend reversed
Leverage rose YoY (Net Debt/EBITDA 0.76x to 1.67x) -- worth monitoring against further earnings weakness
Cement demand is directly tied to Sri Lanka's construction/infrastructure cycle, which this project has no macro data source to forecast

horizon_notes.6m: The FY2024 annual report is now dated (calendar gap to today); an FY2025 filing, if available, should be sourced to check whether the decline reversed.
horizon_notes.1y: Recovery case depends on Sri Lankan construction activity picking back up -- not independently verifiable from this project's data.
horizon_notes.3y: Domestic market leadership is durable, but margin recovery to FY2023 levels (ROE was higher then) is not yet evidenced in the data on file.
horizon_notes.5y: No multi-year cement-cycle data source to assess a longer construction-sector cycle.

interim_updates.note_text: Tokyo Cement's Group revenue grew +26.3% YoY to Rs.15,836mn (Q1 FY2025/26: Rs.12,544mn) and gross profit rose +28.7% to Rs.5,011mn, but Group profit from operations grew only +8.2% to Rs.1,153mn (Q1 FY25/26: Rs.1,065mn) as selling & distribution costs jumped +41.8% (Rs.3,102mn vs Rs.2,188mn) and administrative costs rose +10.1% (Rs.1,017mn vs Rs.924mn), compressing the operating margin from 8.5% to 7.3%. Below the operating line, net finance costs widened from Rs.208mn to Rs.254mn (finance expenses +39.1% to Rs.441mn against finance income +72.0% to Rs.187mn), so PBT grew only +4.9% to Rs.899mn. Tax expense rose +39.9% to Rs.263mn (effective rate up from 22.0% to 29.3%), pulling Group PAT down -5.0% YoY to Rs.635mn and basic EPS down from Rs.1.52 to Rs.1.44. The standalone Company column tells a sharper story: Company profit from operations fell -30.0% and Company PAT fell -55.0% (Rs.203.8mn vs Rs.452.9mn), so the subsidiaries carried the Group's relative resilience this quarter. No segmental note is disclosed (single cement/aggregate business). The filing does not itself split the FY24/25 comparative interim quarter beyond the numbers shown here, so this remains a YoY-only read.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for TKYO -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol (prior rows on file are ANNUAL FY2024/FY2023, a different period_type and not usable for QoQ). Only the filing's own YoY comparative (Q1 FY2025/26) is used here.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline revenue growth (+26%) masks margin compression: operating profit only grew +8% and PAT fell -5% YoY because selling/distribution and admin costs outgrew sales and finance costs widened -- and the standalone Company's profit nearly halved (-55%) while subsidiaries offset the decline at Group level, so the Group number overstates how the core cement business itself performed this quarter.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.15,836mn, +26.3% YoY, but gross margin held roughly flat at 31.6% (vs 31.0%)
Selling & distribution expenses +41.8% YoY (Rs.3,102mn vs Rs.2,188mn) outpaced revenue growth
Group operating margin compressed to 7.3% from 8.5% a year earlier
Finance expenses +39.1% YoY to Rs.441mn while finance income rose +72.0% to Rs.187mn; net finance cost widened to Rs.254mn from Rs.208mn
Effective tax rate rose to 29.3% from 22.0%, amplifying the PAT decline despite a PBT increase
Company (standalone) PAT fell -55.0% YoY to Rs.203.8mn vs Group PAT -5.0% to Rs.635.4mn -- subsidiaries cushioned the Group result
key_drivers: Cost inflation in selling & distribution (+41.8%) and administrative expenses (+10.1%) outgrew the 26.3% revenue increase, compressing operating margin
Net finance cost widened by Rs.46mn YoY (finance expenses +39.1% against finance income +72.0%), trimming PBT growth to +4.9% despite an 8.2% rise in operating profit

Standalone Company operating profit fell -30.0% YoY while Group operating profit rose +8.2%, indicating the subsidiaries (Tokyo Eastern Cement, Tokyo Super Aggregate, Tokyo Supermix) drove the Group-level growth
Effective tax rate rose from 22.0% to 29.3% Group-wide, amplifying the PAT decline relative to the modest PBT increase
